newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates rise on pre-holiday tightness.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates rise on pre-holiday tightness.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates rose sharply in thin pre-holiday trading as banks tried to maintain higher cash levels for withdrawals during two major festivals starting on Friday, dealers said on Thursday.

They said only short-term interbank money was being traded and the rise was due to expectations of the market remaining tight for up to two weeks after the Chinese New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivals.
One-week money was at 8.30/50 percent against 7.10/20, two-week at 7.80/8.00 against 7.20/30 and three-week at 7.60/80 against 7.30/35.
One-month and three-month money were trading at 7.38/40 percent against 7.25/30 and 7.30/35, respectively, on Wednesday, the dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate, which will last up to next Wednesday, was steady at 8.3/5 percent. Malaysian banks are closed for the twin celebrations from Friday through Tuesday.
They said the rise in rates was despite the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue.
"The market is tight because banks have high cash levels for the ATMs (automated teller machines)," a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur said.
"Even after the festivals, people believe it will take about two weeks for the money to come back into the system," he said.
They said rough estimates suggest over three billion ringgit had been withdrawn from the banking system for the festivals.
They said banks were being cautious and mainly squaring up positions ahead of the festivals.
